MHA has separate keys and values for every query head. MQA shares one KV head across all query heads; GQA shares each KV head within a group. Thus MQA/GQA reduce cached state and decode-time KV reads, at a possible quality cost. Query-head count and attention score work can remain unchanged. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.13245)

$$M_{KV}=2BLSH_{KV}d_hb.$$

Here $b$ is bytes per scalar; the factor 2 counts keys and values. MLA instead caches a compressed latent representation plus positional information and uses compatible projections to recover attention behavior. Its saving is not simply “one KV head”: account for latent and positional dimensions and implementation details. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.19437) These methods primarily relieve memory capacity/bandwidth pressure during decoding; they do not remove autoregressive dependence or make all attention computation constant-time.
